## 1. Historical Context

### 1.1 Origins of Backpropagation

```
Timeline of Key Developments:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1960s  - Chain rule formalized in control theory (Kelley, Bryson)
1974   - Paul Werbos proposes backpropagation for neural networks (PhD thesis)
1980s  - Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams rediscover and popularize the algorithm
1986   - "Learning Representations by Back-propagating Errors" published
1990s  - Backpropagation becomes standard training method
2010s+ - Deep learning revolution; backprop remains foundational
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

### 1.2 Key Contributors

| Researcher | Year | Contribution |
|------------|------|--------------|
| Paul Werbos | 1974 | First formulation for neural networks |
| David Rumelhart | 1986 | Popularized the algorithm |
| Geoffrey Hinton | 1986 | Co-developed with Rumelhart |
| David Parker | 1985 | Independently discovered the algorithm |
| Yann LeCun | 1989 | Applied to convolutional networks |

### 1.3 Why Backpropagation Matters

```
Before Backprop (1960s-1980s):
├── Hand-coded features
├── Limited to shallow networks
└── Training was impractical for deep networks

After Backprop (1986+):
├── Automatic feature learning
├── Scalable to deeper networks  
└── Enabled the deep learning revolution
```

## 2. The Forward Pass

### 2.1 Basic Neural Network Structure

```
                    INPUT        HIDDEN        OUTPUT
                    
                   ┌───┐        ┌───┐
              x₁ ─┤   │──w₁₁──┤   │
                   │   │        │   │
              x₂ ─┤  W¹├──w₁₂──┤   │
                   │   │        │   │
              x₃ ─┤   │──w₁₃──┤   │
                   └───┘        └───┘
                              ╱ ╲ ╱ ╲
                             ╱   ╲
                            ╱     ╲
                           ▼       ▼
                         ┌───┐   ┌───┐
                         │   │   │   │
                         │ W²│   │ W²│
                         │   │   │   │
                         └───┘   └───┘
                           │       │
                           ▼       ▼
                          ŷ₁      ŷ₂
```

### 2.2 Mathematical Representation

For a network with **L** layers:

```
Forward Pass Equations:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For layer l (l = 1, 2, ..., L):

    z^[l] = W^[l] · a^[l-1] + b^[l]      (pre-activation)
    
    a^[l] = σ(z^[l])                      (activation)
    
Where:
    - W^[l] : Weight matrix of shape (n^[l], n^[l-1])
    - b^[l] : Bias vector of shape (n^[l], 1)
    - z^[l] : Pre-activation of layer l
    - a^[l] : Activation of layer l (a^[0] = x input)
    - σ    : Activation function
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

### 2.3
